meta.title: Privacy
meta.description: What this product stores, what it does not, how long it keeps it, and how to discard it.

heading: What this product stores
opening: This product has no accounts, no sign-in and no user profiles. It cannot tell who you are, and it is not built so that it could later. What follows is the whole of what is written down, why each thing is written, and what you can do about it.

purpose.heading: Why anything is kept at all
purpose.body: One reason: so that an answer can be checked. A product that says where every claim came from has to be able to show, afterwards, which passages it read, which version of which document those passages were in, and whether it abstained. That is the record. Nothing here is kept for analytics, for personalisation, or to improve a model.
purpose.limitation: Purpose limitation. What is written is written for that check and used for nothing else.
purpose.minimisation: Data minimisation. The record answers "did this behave the way it says it does". None of the questions it answers needs your words, so your words are not in it.
purpose.consent: Consent. The core function — asking a question and getting a cited answer — runs on what is described here and asks for nothing more. Anything beyond it is asked for separately, names what it is, and waits.

stored.heading: What is written down
stored.intro: One row per query, in a local database, appended and never edited.
stored.sessionIdWhy: A random value this tab made up. It ties your question to the feedback you leave about the answer, and it is what the rate limit counts. It lives in this tab and dies with it.
stored.questionHashWhy: A one-way digest, not the text. It lets the same question asked twice be recognised as the same question. The words cannot be recovered from it.
stored.passagesWhy: Which pieces of which documents the answer was built from. This is the part that makes a citation checkable rather than decorative.
stored.versionsWhy: So an answer given today can be traced to the exact instruction and the exact source set that produced it, after both have moved on.
stored.outcome: Confidence, whether it abstained, and why
stored.outcomeWhy: So a claim that the system abstains when retrieval is weak can be checked against how often it actually did.
stored.timing: Latency, and counts of what was stripped or dropped
stored.timingWhy: How long it took, how many instruction-like spans were removed from source text, and how many claims lost their citation and were removed from the answer.
stored.consentEventsWhy: If you ever agree to reach a source with your own credentials, that decision and its time are recorded, and so is withdrawing it.

notStored.heading: What is not written down
notStored.intro: These are not fields that are left empty. They are not columns.
notStored.question: The text of your question.
notStored.note: Any note you type into the feedback box. The box is offered, the verdict is kept, and the note is discarded — a note nobody can act on is a liability rather than a feature.
notStored.identity: Your name, email address, organisation or any other identifier. You are never asked for one.
notStored.ip: Your IP address. The rate limit counts the session id instead, precisely so an address never has to be held.
notStored.credentials: Any credential of yours. This product never holds, stores or transmits a password or an API key belonging to you, for any source, at any point.
notStored.verify: This is checkable rather than promised: the audit table's columns are listed on the development viewer, read from the schema that creates the table.

sharing.heading: Who else sees it
sharing.body: Nobody. The record is a file on the machine running this product. There is no analytics script, no advertising network, no error-reporting service and no third-party tag anywhere in this interface — the content policy on this page forbids loading one.
sharing.model: If a deployment is configured to use a hosted model, the question text and the retrieved passages are sent to that provider to write the answer, and the answer's own status line names which generator ran. With no key configured — the default — no text leaves the machine at all.
sharing.escalate: The handoff summary is assembled in your browser and copied to your clipboard. It is not sent anywhere. There is no expert network behind it, and nothing is queued.

retention.heading: How long it is kept
retention.session: The session id: until this tab closes.
retention.rows: The audit rows: for as long as the deployment keeps them. They are append-only, so a row is never quietly rewritten — an operator who removes them removes them wholesale, and the record does not pretend otherwise.
retention.language: Your language choice: until you change it or clear your browser storage. It is a preference, not a record of what you asked.

deletion.heading: Discarding what links to you
deletion.body: There is no account to close, because there is no account. What ties one row to another is the session id, and that id is in this tab and nowhere else. Discarding it is not a gesture towards a deletion path — it is the whole of one. The rows that remain hold no identity, no address and none of your words, so there is nothing left in them to connect to a person.
deletion.confirm: Discard it? The next question starts fresh, with no history and no consents.
deletion.done: Discarded. This tab now has a new session id, and the earlier one is gone.
deletion.keepsLanguage: Your language choice is kept. That is a preference you set, not a record of what you asked.

consent.heading: Sources that would need your say-so
consent.body: Some registries and databases are reached only through a subscription that belongs to the reader, not to this product. Those are never fetched here, under any setting. If one is ever used, it is used with your own credentials, one named source at a time, after you have said so — never under a blanket agreement.
consent.none: No source in the current set needs your credentials. This sentence is read from the source manifest, not typed here, so it stops being shown the moment one is added.
consent.some_one: {{count}} source in the current set would need your credentials.
consent.some_other: {{count}} sources in the current set would need your credentials.
consent.unavailable: The access log could not be reached, so this cannot be stated. Rather than assume, it says nothing.
consent.dialogBody: {{source}} is published by {{organization}} and is not fetched by this product. To search it for this question, your own subscription is used: the request goes out under your credentials, from your session.
consent.dialogHolds: This product does not see, hold or store the credential itself.
consent.dialogScope: This applies to {{source}} only, for this session only. It does not extend to any other source, and you can withdraw it below at any time.
consent.dialogLogged: Agreeing is recorded in your access log, with the time, and so is withdrawing.
consent.failed: That was not recorded. Nothing has been agreed to.

log.heading: Your access log
log.intro: Every consent decision this session has made, newest first. Withdrawing does not remove the grant that came before it: it happened, and a log that erased it could not show when the access was held.
log.empty: Nothing has been agreed to in this session.
log.unavailable: The access log could not be reached. Nothing is being shown rather than a guess at what it holds.

basis.heading: The basis for holding it
basis.body: The audit record is what makes a source-cited product auditable, which is the function you came here for; it is held for that and nothing else. Consent is asked for separately, and only where something goes beyond that function — reaching a source with your own credentials is the one case in this design. Where consent is asked, it names the source, it is given by an action you take, and withdrawing it is on this page and takes effect immediately.
basis.notAdvice: None of this makes the product an authority. It does not grant rights, approve products, issue licences or replace a professional adviser.
